messages.subject: mapreduce job with multiple inputs
parts:
Hi,
I read that the argument ifolder to rhmr can be a vector of strings. I surmise that this allows to read multiple files in one job. My question is: when in the mapper, is there a way to tell if a key value pair comes from one input or the other? If you haven't guessed it already, I am trying to implement a join (relational, nothing to deal with rhjoin). Thanks


Antonio

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] mapreduce job with multiple inputs
parts:
Thanks, that was helpful. This is how the join looks like. Besides what it does, which is very useful to combine two datasets, folks might be interested in passing argument (functions in this case) to the map and reduce expressions using eval(substitute(expr, list(var1 = val1 ...))). Less than minimal testing, use at your own risk. Why didn't I use the partitioner as it is customary for mr joins? Because of some limitations in the partitioner (type constraints). Therefore this is going to break when one key is present too many times. I hope to fix it if restrictions on partitioner are eased. Also, doesn't work as self-join. Comments, corrections and improvements appreciated.

function(ileftfolder, 
         irightfolder,
         ofolder,
         map.left.key = function(k, v) k,
         map.right.key = function(k, v) k,
         map.right.value = function(k, v) v,
         map.left.value = function(k, v) v,
         reduce.key = function(k, vl, vr) k,
         reduce.value = function (k, vl, vr) c(vl, vr)){
  rhex(
       rhmr(
            map = eval(
              substitute(
                         expression({
                           lapply(seq_along(map.keys), function(i) {
                             mapcollect = function(k,v, kfun, vfun, left) rhcollect(kfun(k,v), list(value = vfun(k,v), left = left))
                             if(length(grep(paste("^file:", ileftfolder, sep = ""), Sys.getenv("mapred.input.file")))) {
                               mapcollect(map.keys[[i]], map.values[[i]], map.left.key, map.left.value, T)}
                             else {
                               mapcollect(map.keys[[i]], map.values[[i]], map.right.key, map.right.value, F)}
                           })}),
                         list(map.left.key = map.left.key,
                              map.right.key = map.right.key,
                              map.right.value = map.right.value,
                              map.left.value = map.left.value,
                              ileftfolder = ileftfolder))),
            reduce = eval(
              substitute(
                         expression(
                             pre = {
                               reduce.split = function(values, left) lapply(values[which(lapply(values, function(x) x$left) == left)], function(x) x$value)
                               all.values = c()},
                             reduce = {
                               all.values = c(all.values, reduce.values)},
                             post = {
                               reduce.values.left = reduce.split(all.values, T)
                               reduce.values.right = reduce.split(all.values, F)
                               lapply(reduce.values.left,                                      
                                      function(x) lapply(reduce.values.right,
                                                         function(y) rhcollect(reduce.key.fun(reduce.key, x, y),
                                                                               reduce.value(reduce.key, x, y))))
                             }),
                         list(reduce.key.fun = reduce.key,
                              reduce.value = reduce.value
                              ))),
            combiner = F,
            inout = c('sequence','sequence'),
            ifolder=c(ileftfolder,irightfolder),
            ofolder= ofolder
            )
       )
}
